title: Accessible Group Wedding Weekend with Hotel Double-Booking Cascade

scenario.description: A family of 6 (including one wheelchair-dependent elderly member) is traveling to Portland for a wedding event. The wedding ceremony is on Saturday, rehearsal dinner Friday evening, and family gathering Sunday morning. After booking, the hotel confirms they made a double-booking error and must relocate the group.

dynamic_events.description: The hotel contacts you urgently: they double-booked your accessible room and must relocate your entire group. New hotel has ONE accessible room (fits 3 people) but you need 6 people accommodated total. Option 1: Book new hotel accessible room + non-accessible rooms elsewhere in wedding block (may be across town). Option 2: Split the group across two nearby hotels (one accessible, one standard). Option 3: Use available Airbnb's and hotels (may not all be wheelchair accessible for pickup/dropoff). You have 2 hours to decide.
resolution_requirements: Find alternative accommodation for all 6 people that maintains wheelchair accessibility
If splitting across hotels: arrange ground transportation between them for Friday dinner, Saturday ceremony, Sunday brunch
Verify all mandatory event venues are accessible from new hotel(s)
Verify all restaurant reservations near new hotel location(s) or adjust if locations change significantly
Ensure elderly family member accessibility accommodations are preserved (bathroom accessibility, room location, etc.)
Keep total accommodation cost increase within budget (max 5500 total for trip)
Preserve rental car or rideshare arrangements

expected_challenges: Accessibility constraint must be verified not just for primary accommodation but for ground transportation between multiple hotels if split
Cascading effect: hotel relocation → ground transport replanning → restaurant location verification → accessibility of all venues
Group dynamics: must keep 6 people reasonably coordinated across multiple accommodations
Wheelchair accessibility + elderly needs create compound constraint
Late-notice replanning (2-hour deadline) simulates real-world travel stress
Multiple mandatory events with specific times and accessibility requirements
notes: HARD task because: (1) Group travel with accessibility constraints, (2) Single disruption (overbooking) cascades to 5+ components, (3) Agent must reason about spatial/temporal dependencies between hotels, events, and transportation, (4) Multiple family member needs to coordinate, (5) Accessibility verification must be applied across entire itinerary, not just accommodation.
